target_customer: Frontier AI labs buying training data and RL environments
problem: Labs need expert-quality training data and environments (starting with competition math) to improve reasoning and AI research agents.
business_model: Sells datasets and RL environments to AI labs; expert contractor network
product_category: AI training data and RL environments

founders.name: Jun Park
founders.background_notes: Former professional Valorant player per the YC page and launch post.

founders.name: Ibrakhim Ustelbay
previous_startups: Headstarter (AI interviewer, 100k+ users per the launch post)

competitors.name: Mercor, Surge, Handshake, Turing
competitors.what: Human data vendors that also sell RL environments
competitors.traction_then: Named by TechCrunch as moving into environments

competitors.name: Scale AI
competitors.traction_then: Lost ground after Meta's $14B investment per TechCrunch

technical_complexity.rationale: Building verifiable math environments with Lean formalization needs expert talent and tooling, but it is data work rather than a research breakthrough.

defensibility.rationale: Expert network and lab relationships help, but labs build in-house and large vendors compete.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large vendors added RL environment offerings in 2025; no action against hillclimb found.

market_need_then: In 2025 labs shifted spending to RL environments and expert data; TechCrunch reported in September 2025 that Silicon Valley was betting heavily on environments.

branding.domain_note: Launch page used hillclimb.com; a later copy of the page shows hillclimb.ing. Which is current is unconfirmed.
branding.community_and_virality: Co-authorship with Nous Research mathematicians on a math model, per the YC launch post.

brand_strength.rationale: Name evokes optimization but is shared with unrelated firms; little brand coverage found.

outcome_analysis: Active as of 2026-11 and too early to call. The team shows a lab partnership with Nous Research and a math expert network, but vendors with far more capital sell the same product and labs are in-housing, so durability depends on keeping scarce expert supply.
notes: Standout.work and Extruct list a $500K seed with Y Combinator as investor; other aggregators say pre-seed dated Oct or Dec 2025, so date and stage conflict and the date is left null. The round rests on databases. The company site says it is backed by Tier 1 VCs, Jeff Dean, Paul Graham and others with no amounts, so a gap may exist. Competitor list comes from a general RL environments article, not math-specific coverage.
